```{r}
#| label: config
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Fits from the migrant analysis script (forest-reference variants, 2026-11-15): forest as the reference habitat, one intercept per survey period with the two 2016-17 periods merged (2025-26 reference), team-specific warm-up slopes and the free spatial range prior
fit_dir <- "Derived/Rdata/Model_output/Temporal/Single_species"
# Single-species fits only for migrants detected often enough outside forest to estimate habitat contrasts
species_ss <- c("Setophaga_striata", "Setophaga_ruticilla", "Piranga_rubra")
# Radii of landscape canopy cover carried into the base models (user, 2026-11-15): S. striata's single-species profile minimum and the community's; S. ruticilla and P. rubra without canopy, as no radius was supported for them (user, 2026-11-16)
striata_radius <- 5000
comm_radius <- 3000
# Base models (2026-11-16): the forest-reference variants plus landscape canopy cover at the chosen radius, with an arrival-period indicator in place of day of season (user, 2026-11-16: with period intercepts the linear day-of-season slope came almost only from forest in October-December 2016 vs March 2017); arrival ends 1 December, and the multi-species model has doubled chains (its silvopasture among-species variance mixed poorly at the standard length)
ss_tags <- c(Setophaga_striata = paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", striata_radius, "_arr_free"), Setophaga_ruticilla = "oct15_team_day_fref_arr_free", Piranga_rubra = "oct15_team_day_fref_arr_free")
ms_tag <- paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", comm_radius, "_arr_free_ig11_long")
# The same base models with a linear day of season or without any season term, and the multi-species model with arrival ending 1 November, for the comparison of season terms
ss_day_tags <- c(Setophaga_striata = paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", striata_radius, "_free"), Setophaga_ruticilla = "oct15_team_day_fref_free", Piranga_rubra = "oct15_team_day_fref_free")
ms_day_tag <- paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", comm_radius, "_free_ig11")
ss_noday_tags <- c(Setophaga_striata = paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", striata_radius, "_noday_free"), Setophaga_ruticilla = "oct15_team_day_fref_noday_free", Piranga_rubra = "oct15_team_day_fref_noday_free")
ms_noday_tag <- paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", comm_radius, "_noday_free_ig11")
ms_arrnov_tag <- paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", comm_radius, "_arrnov_free_ig11_long")
# S. striata without canopy (with the arrival indicator), for the WAIC of its canopy ring in the base model
striata_nc_arr_tag <- "oct15_team_day_fref_arr_free"
# The same models without canopy and with day of season, the base of the sensitivity variants below (habitat-by-rainfall, prior variance, reference level, silvopasture's distance slope, silvopasture split), which were not refit (user, 2026-11-16: sensitivity checks are rerun before publication)
ss_tag <- "oct15_team_day_fref_free"
ms_nc_tag <- "oct15_team_day_fref_free_ig11"
# Habitat-by-annual-rainfall variants of the same models (the multi-species one with 200,000-iteration chains)
ss_rain_tag <- "oct15_team_day_fref_rain_free"
ms_rain_tag <- "oct15_team_day_fref_rain_free_ig11_mid"
# Prior sensitivity: variance of the normal prior on the occupancy coefficients (single-species) or on their community-level means (multi-species), 1 and 10 instead of spOccupancy's default 2.72
prior_vars <- c(1, 10)
# Scale of effect of landscape canopy cover (2026-11-15): ring profiles and spatial-effect summaries, written by the migrant analysis script's ring_compare section
ring_csv <- "Derived/Excels/Migrant_ss_ring_comparison.csv"
ring_loadings_csv <- "Derived/Excels/Migrant_ms_ring_spatial_loadings.csv"
# Non-spatial check of the community radius (2026-11-15 night): location random effect in place of the spatial factor, with and without canopy
ms_nonsp_tag <- "oct15_team_day_fref_nonsp_ig11"
ms_ring_nonsp_tag <- paste0("oct15_team_day_fref_r", comm_radius, "_nonsp_ig11")
# Migrants outside Meta (user, 2026-11-16): in-season point counts from all ecoregions in the sibling wrangling repository, and AVONET long-distance migrants from its trait table
wrangling_dir <- "../Ssp-bird-data-wrangling/Derived/Excels/"
# AVONET long-distance migrants that are not Nearctic-Neotropical migrants in Colombia (resident or austral-migrant populations, or breeding only in Middle America), excluded as for the Meta migrant list
not_nearctic <- c("Chrysolampis mosquitus", "Coccyzus lansbergi", "Elaenia pallatangae", "Empidonomus varius", "Falco sparverius", "Myiodynastes maculatus", "Myiopagis viridicata", "Pyrocephalus rubinus", "Tyrannus savana", "Vireo flavoviridis")
# Species whose Colombian records may include resident populations (marked in the table)
mixed_status <- c("Setophaga petechia", "Vireo olivaceus")
# The tag must be followed directly by the fit date, so e.g. "fref_free" does not also match "fref_free_short"
fit_path <- \(sp, tag) list.files(fit_dir, paste0("^Occ_mod_", sp, "_", tag, "_\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\.rds$"), full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(all(imap_int(ss_tags, \(tag, sp) length(fit_path(sp, tag))) == 1), all(map_int(c(ss_tag, striata_nc_arr_tag), \(tag) length(fit_path("Setophaga_striata", tag))) == 1), all(map_int(c(ms_tag, ms_day_tag, ms_nc_tag, ms_nonsp_tag, ms_ring_nonsp_tag), \(tag) length(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", tag))) == 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: data
# The migrant analysis script's data section (no fits run without fit names on the command line) gives the season window, teams, periods, day-of-season scaling, covariate scaling and the multi-species detection array
invisible(capture.output(suppressMessages(source("Scripts/Migrant_occupancy.R", local = TRUE))))
species_label <- \(sp) str_replace(sp, "_", " ")
fits <- map(set_names(species_ss), \(sp) readRDS(fit_path(sp, ss_tags[[sp]])))
ms_fit <- readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", ms_tag))
# Base models without canopy, against which the sensitivity variants are compared
striata_nc <- readRDS(fit_path("Setophaga_striata", ss_tag))
ms_fit_nc <- readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", ms_nc_tag))
# WAIC of the base models with and without day of season, and the largest change in any silvopasture contrast (logit scale, posterior medians) when it is dropped
waic_of <- \(m) spOccupancy::waicOcc(m, by.sp = FALSE)[["WAIC"]]
season_waic <- c(map(set_names(species_ss), \(sp) c(day = waic_of(readRDS(fit_path(sp, ss_day_tags[[sp]]))), none = waic_of(readRDS(fit_path(sp, ss_noday_tags[[sp]]))), arrival = waic_of(fits[[sp]]))),
                 list(Community = c(day = waic_of(readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", ms_day_tag))), none = waic_of(readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", ms_noday_tag))), arrival = waic_of(ms_fit))))
# Multi-species fit with arrival ending 1 November: among-species variance Rhat of the arrival coefficient and the species never detected before 1 November
ms_arrnov <- readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", ms_arrnov_tag))
arrnov_rhat <- ms_arrnov$rhat$tau.sq.beta[colnames(ms_arrnov$tau.sq.beta.samples) == "Arrival_nov1"]
arrnov_sp <- apply(as.matrix(ms_arrnov$beta.samples)[, paste0("Arrival_nov1-", Migrants)], 2, median) %>% set_names(Migrants)
# Arrival effects in the base models (logit scale)
arrival_ss <- map(fits, \(m) m$beta.samples[, "Arrival"])
n_visits <- sum(!is.na(ss_l$y))
n_locations <- dim(ss_l$y)[1]
habitat <- as.character(ss_l$occ.covs$Habitat)
surveyed_lp <- apply(ss_l$y, 1:2, \(v) any(!is.na(v)))
lp_by_habitat <- tapply(rowSums(surveyed_lp), habitat, sum)
farm <- Stacked_oc$Farm_name[match(Site_levels[Keep_site], Stacked_oc$Id_survey_no_dc)]
farms_by_habitat <- tapply(farm, habitat, n_distinct)
season_start_date <- format(as.Date(Season_start - 1, origin = "2025-01-01"), "%d %B")
season_end_date <- format(as.Date(Season_end - 1, origin = "2025-01-01"), "%d %B")
# In-season detections and location-periods with a detection by habitat, per migrant
detections <- apply(ms_l$y, 1, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
hab_lp <- matrix(habitat, nrow(surveyed_lp), ncol(surveyed_lp))
det_lp_by_habitat <- map(set_names(Migrants), \(sp) tapply(c(apply(ms_l$y[sp, , , ], 1:2, \(v) any(v == 1, na.rm = TRUE))), c(hab_lp), sum))
# Detections outside the season window (mostly September-October passage), per migrant
off_season <- map_dbl(set_names(Migrants), \(sp) sum(Migrants_l$y[sp, , , ][!is.na(Julian) & Julian > Season_end & Julian < Season_start], na.rm = TRUE))
# Formatting helpers: posterior median with 95% CrI (tables, captions), and with the posterior probability that the quantity is positive (text)
ci <- \(x, digits = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"), median(x), quantile(x, 0.025), quantile(x, 0.975))
est <- \(x, digits = 2) paste0(ci(x, digits), ", P(>0) = ", sprintf("%.2f", mean(x > 0)))
# MCMC and spatial settings from the migrant analysis script's configuration
n_iter <- Mcmc$n.batch * Batch_length
n_iter_long <- Mcmc_long$n.batch * Batch_length
n_iter_mid <- Mcmc_mid$n.batch * Batch_length
free_range_km <- Range_priors$free / 1000
dist_sd_m <- Dist_sd$SD
ssp_scale <- filter(Scaling, Process == "occupancy", Covariate == "ssp")
# Canopy cover in the community's ring, standardised over the surveyed location-periods of the 98-species data as in the migrant analysis script
canopy_scale <- Ring_rows %>% filter(Radius_m == comm_radius) %>% summarise(Mean = mean(Canopy_cover_ring), SD = sd(Canopy_cover_ring))
prec_scale <- filter(Scaling, Process == "occupancy", Covariate == "Tot_prec")
# First Meta detection and the run of non-detection visits before it, from the full survey tables (computed in the session of 2026-11-14, not by the migrant analysis script)
first_detection <- "8 October 2019"
n_visits_before_first <- 439
# Survey periods as written in the text
period_text <- paste(c(`16-17.Early` = "October-December 2016", `16-17.Late` = "March 2017", `19.Early` = "November 2019", `25-26.Early` = "January-February 2026")[Periods_kept], collapse = ", ")
```

```{r}
#| label: summaries
## Species coefficients with the single-species names: single-species fits, each migrant's coefficients from the multi-species fit, and the community means
ss_beta <- map(fits, \(m) m$beta.samples)
species_beta <- \(m) map(set_names(Migrants), \(sp) {
  b <- as.matrix(m$beta.samples)[, str_ends(colnames(m$beta.samples), paste0("-", sp)), drop = FALSE]
  colnames(b) <- str_remove(colnames(b), paste0("-", sp, "$"))
  b
})
ms_beta <- species_beta(ms_fit)
comm_beta <- as.matrix(ms_fit$beta.comm.samples)
## Habitat contrasts on the logit scale (forest is the reference level; they do not depend on the other covariates in the additive model)
contrasts_of <- \(b) list(`Silvopasture vs pasture` = b[, "Habitat_frefSsp"] - b[, "Habitat_frefPastizales"], `Forest vs pasture` = -b[, "Habitat_frefPastizales"], `Silvopasture vs forest` = b[, "Habitat_frefSsp"])
ss_contrasts <- map(ss_beta, contrasts_of)
ms_contrasts <- map(ms_beta, contrasts_of)
comm_contrasts <- contrasts_of(comm_beta)
striata_nc_contrasts <- contrasts_of(striata_nc$beta.samples)
## Convergence: largest Rhat of the single-species fits, community-level Rhat of the multi-species fit and its species coefficients above 1.1
max_rhat_ss <- max(map_dbl(fits, \(m) max(unlist(m$rhat), na.rm = TRUE)))
max_rhat_comm <- max(unlist(ms_fit$rhat[c("beta.comm", "alpha.comm", "tau.sq.beta", "tau.sq.alpha")]), na.rm = TRUE)
n_sp_rhat <- sum(unlist(ms_fit$rhat[c("beta", "alpha")]) > 1.1, na.rm = TRUE)

## Prediction conditions: the reference period (2025-26, surveyed in all three habitats), at its mean day of season for the sensitivity fits that still include it, at the forest edge, other covariates at their means, spatial random effect at zero (an average location)
ref_col <- which(Periods_kept == Period_ref)
day_ref <- mean(ss_l$occ.covs$Day_season[surveyed_lp[, ref_col], ref_col])
day_to_date <- \(d) as.Date(Season_start - 1, origin = "2025-01-01") + round(d * Day_sd + Day_mean)
day_ref_date <- format(day_to_date(day_ref), "%d %B")
hab_labels <- c(Pastizales = "Pasture", Ssp = "Silvopasture", Bosque = "Forest")
hab_colors <- c(Pasture = "#eda100", Silvopasture = "#6250d6", Forest = "#008300")
## Occupancy draws for one habitat; distances in SD units, silvopasture cover and day of season (fits that include it) on the model's standardized scales
pred_occ <- function(b, hab, dist_open = 0, dist_inside = 0, ssp = 0, day = day_ref, prec = 0, canopy = 0) {
  eta <- b[, "(Intercept)"] + b[, "Dist_open"] * dist_open + b[, "Dist_inside"] * dist_inside + b[, "ssp"] * ssp + b[, "Tot_prec"] * prec
  if ("Day_season" %in% colnames(b)) eta <- eta + b[, "Day_season"] * day
  # Fits with landscape canopy cover (one ring), standardized over that ring
  canopy_term <- grep("^Canopy_r", colnames(b), value = TRUE)
  if (length(canopy_term)) eta <- eta + b[, canopy_term] * canopy
  if (hab != "Bosque") eta <- eta + b[, paste0("Habitat_fref", hab)]
  # Habitat-by-rainfall fits: the habitat's difference from the forest rainfall slope
  if (paste0("Habitat_fref", hab, ":Tot_prec") %in% colnames(b)) eta <- eta + b[, paste0("Habitat_fref", hab, ":Tot_prec")] * prec
  plogis(eta)
}
## Occupancy draws at one value of one covariate, given in display units (m: signed distance to the forest edge; ssp: % within 300 m; prec: annual rainfall in mm; canopy: % canopy cover in the community's ring), others at the prediction conditions
pred_at <- function(b, hab_label, var, x) {
  hab <- names(hab_labels)[hab_labels == hab_label]
  switch(var,
    m = pred_occ(b, hab, dist_open = pmax(x, 0) / dist_sd_m, dist_inside = pmax(-x, 0) / dist_sd_m),
    ssp = pred_occ(b, hab, ssp = (x - ssp_scale$Mean) / ssp_scale$SD),
    prec = pred_occ(b, hab, prec = (x - prec_scale$Mean) / prec_scale$SD),
    canopy = pred_occ(b, hab, canopy = (x - canopy_scale$Mean) / canopy_scale$SD))
}
summarise_draws <- \(tbl) tbl %>% mutate(med = map_dbl(draws, median), lcl = map_dbl(draws, quantile, 0.025), ucl = map_dbl(draws, quantile, 0.975)) %>% select(-draws)

## Table 1: in-season detections of every migrant in the multi-species model
data_tbl <- tibble(sp = Migrants) %>%
  mutate(Species = paste0("*", species_label(sp), "*", if_else(sp %in% species_ss, "\\*", "")), `In-season detections` = detections[sp],
         Detected = map_chr(sp, \(s) paste(det_lp_by_habitat[[s]][c("Pastizales", "Ssp", "Bosque")], collapse = " / "))) %>%
  select(-sp) %>%
  # Non-breaking spaces keep the habitat order on one line when the header wraps
  rename("Detected location-periods (pasture\u00a0/\u00a0silvopasture\u00a0/\u00a0forest)" = Detected)

## Occupancy by habitat, single-species fits
occ_by_habitat <- imap(ss_beta, \(b, sp) tibble(Species = species_label(sp), code = names(hab_labels), draws = map(code, \(h) pred_occ(b, h)))) %>%
  list_rbind() %>%
  summarise_draws() %>%
  mutate(Habitat = factor(hab_labels[code], hab_labels), Species = factor(Species, species_label(species_ss)))
## Pasture occupancy, single- vs multi-species, in the fits without canopy, as the forest-reference fits that replaced the earlier pasture-reference fit (the level every contrast against pasture is measured from)
pasture_occ <- map(set_names(species_ss), \(sp) list(ss = pred_occ(if (sp == "Setophaga_striata") striata_nc$beta.samples else ss_beta[[sp]], "Pastizales"), ms = pred_occ(species_beta(ms_fit_nc)[[sp]], "Pastizales")))

## Silvopasture contrasts per species, single- vs multi-species, with the community mean
compare_tbl <- bind_rows(
  imap(ss_contrasts, \(d, sp) tibble(Species = species_label(sp), Model = "Single-species", Contrast = names(d), draws = d)) %>% list_rbind(),
  imap(ms_contrasts[species_ss], \(d, sp) tibble(Species = species_label(sp), Model = "Multi-species", Contrast = names(d), draws = d)) %>% list_rbind(),
  tibble(Species = "Community mean", Model = "Multi-species", Contrast = names(comm_contrasts), draws = comm_contrasts)
) %>%
  filter(Contrast != "Forest vs pasture") %>%
  summarise_draws() %>%
  mutate(Species = factor(Species, rev(c(species_label(species_ss), "Community mean"))), Model = factor(Model, c("Single-species", "Multi-species")), Contrast = factor(Contrast, c("Silvopasture vs pasture", "Silvopasture vs forest")))

## Location-period table per species: habitat, signed distance to the forest edge (m; negative inside forest), silvopasture cover within 300 m (%), day of season and posterior mean latent occupancy (z), for the figure points
signed_m <- (ss_l$occ.covs$Dist_open - ss_l$occ.covs$Dist_inside) * dist_sd_m
ssp_pct <- ss_l$occ.covs$ssp * ssp_scale$SD + ssp_scale$Mean
# Annual rainfall is one value per location, recycled down the period columns like habitat
prec_mm <- matrix(as.numeric(ss_l$occ.covs$Tot_prec), nrow(surveyed_lp), ncol(surveyed_lp)) * prec_scale$SD + prec_scale$Mean
canopy_pct <- ss_l$occ.covs[[paste0("Canopy_r", comm_radius)]] * canopy_scale$SD + canopy_scale$Mean
lp_table <- \(z_mean, sp) tibble(Species = species_label(sp), Habitat = hab_labels[c(hab_lp)], m = c(signed_m), ssp = c(ssp_pct), prec = c(prec_mm), canopy = c(canopy_pct), day = c(ss_l$occ.covs$Day_season), z = c(z_mean), surveyed = c(surveyed_lp)) %>%
  filter(surveyed) %>%
  mutate(Habitat = factor(Habitat, hab_labels))
lp_ss <- imap(fits, \(fit, sp) lp_table(apply(fit$z.samples, 2:3, mean), sp)) %>% list_rbind() %>% mutate(Species = factor(Species, species_label(species_ss)))
ss_rain_fits <- map(set_names(species_ss), \(sp) readRDS(fit_path(sp, ss_rain_tag)))
ss_rain_beta <- map(ss_rain_fits, \(m) m$beta.samples)
lp_ss_rain <- imap(ss_rain_fits, \(fit, sp) lp_table(apply(fit$z.samples, 2:3, mean), sp)) %>% list_rbind() %>% mutate(Species = factor(Species, species_label(species_ss)))

## Curve grid: each habitat over its observed range of one covariate (60 points), from a location-period table
curve_grid <- \(lp, var) lp %>%
  summarise(lo = min(.data[[var]]), hi = max(.data[[var]]), .by = any_of(c("Species", "Habitat"))) %>%
  mutate(x = map2(lo, hi, \(lo, hi) seq(lo, hi, length.out = 60))) %>%
  unnest(x) %>%
  select(-lo, -hi)
## Single-species curves (supplement): per species and habitat, from that species' fit
ss_curves <- \(beta_l, lp, var) curve_grid(lp, var) %>%
  mutate(draws = pmap(list(Species, Habitat, x), \(sp, h, x) pred_at(beta_l[[str_replace(sp, " ", "_")]], h, var, x))) %>%
  summarise_draws()
## Location-periods binned along one covariate within habitat, posterior mean latent occupancy, for the figure points
lp_bins <- \(lp, var, width) lp %>%
  mutate(Bin = cut_width(.data[[var]], width, boundary = 0)) %>%
  summarise(x = mean(.data[[var]]), n = n(), z = mean(z), .by = c(Species, Habitat, Bin))
ssp_tbl <- ss_curves(ss_beta, lp_ss, "ssp")
ssp_points <- lp_bins(lp_ss, "ssp", 10)
dist_tbl <- ss_curves(ss_beta, lp_ss, "m")
dist_points <- lp_bins(lp_ss, "m", 50)
rain_tbl <- ss_curves(ss_rain_beta, lp_ss_rain, "prec")
rain_points <- lp_bins(lp_ss_rain, "prec", 200)

## Community-level curves (main text, multi-species fits): within each posterior draw, the mean across the migrants of each species' predicted occupancy, as in the 98-species report; faint lines are each species' posterior median curve
ms_rain <- readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", ms_rain_tag))
ms_rain_beta <- species_beta(ms_rain)
lp_all <- lp_table(NA, species_ss[1]) %>% select(-Species)
context_specs <- tribble(
  ~Panel, ~var, ~beta_l,
  "(a) Annual rainfall (mm)", "prec", ms_rain_beta,
  "(b) Distance to forest edge (m)", "m", ms_beta,
  "(c) Silvopasture within 300 m (%)", "ssp", ms_beta,
  paste0("(d) Canopy cover within ", comm_radius / 1000, " km (%)"), "canopy", ms_beta
)
context_draws <- pmap(context_specs, \(Panel, var, beta_l) curve_grid(lp_all, var) %>%
  mutate(Panel = Panel, sp_draws = map2(Habitat, x, \(h, x) map(beta_l, \(b) pred_at(b, h, var, x))))) %>%
  list_rbind() %>%
  mutate(Panel = factor(Panel, context_specs$Panel))
context_comm <- context_draws %>% mutate(draws = map(sp_draws, \(d) rowMeans(do.call(cbind, d)))) %>% select(-sp_draws) %>% summarise_draws()
context_species <- context_draws %>% mutate(Species = map(sp_draws, names), med = map(sp_draws, \(d) map_dbl(d, median))) %>% select(-sp_draws) %>% unnest(c(Species, med))
## Community-level means of the species' slopes (logit scale, per SD), and each habitat's rainfall slope in the rainfall fit (forest slope plus the habitat's difference)
comm_rain <- as.matrix(ms_rain$beta.comm.samples)
rain_slopes <- \(b) list(Forest = b[, "Tot_prec"], Pasture = b[, "Tot_prec"] + b[, "Habitat_frefPastizales:Tot_prec"], Silvopasture = b[, "Tot_prec"] + b[, "Habitat_frefSsp:Tot_prec"])
comm_rain_slopes <- rain_slopes(comm_rain)
ss_rain_slopes <- map(ss_rain_beta, rain_slopes)

## Prior sensitivity (S. striata single-species and the multi-species model): silvopasture contrasts under each prior variance, with the default 2.72 from the base fits without canopy
striata_prior <- map(set_names(prior_vars), \(v) contrasts_of(readRDS(fit_path("Setophaga_striata", paste0(ss_tag, "_bvar", v)))$beta.samples))
ms_prior <- map(set_names(prior_vars), \(v) readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", paste0(ms_nc_tag, "_bvar", v))))
comm_prior <- map(ms_prior, \(m) contrasts_of(as.matrix(m$beta.comm.samples)))
rhat_ssp_var <- map_dbl(ms_prior, \(m) m$rhat$tau.sq.beta[colnames(m$tau.sq.beta.samples) == "Habitat_frefSsp"])

## Reference-level check (S. striata single-species): the same model with pasture as the reference, and the earlier pasture-reference fit with the two 2016-17 periods separate and a quadratic in day of season
striata_pref <- readRDS(fit_path("Setophaga_striata", "oct15_team_day_pref_free"))$beta.samples
striata_old <- readRDS(fit_path("Setophaga_striata", "oct15_team_day_period_free"))$beta.samples
## Multi-species variants: silvopasture's own slope with distance outside forest, and silvopasture split into live fence and dispersed trees; WAIC on the same data as the base model, against the base model without canopy
ms_dist <- readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", "oct15_team_day_fref_dist_free_ig11"))
ms_split <- readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", "oct15_team_day_fref_split_free_ig11"))
waic <- map_dbl(list(base = ms_fit_nc, dist = ms_dist, split = ms_split, rain = ms_rain), \(m) spOccupancy::waicOcc(m, by.sp = FALSE)[["WAIC"]])
rhat_comm <- \(m) max(unlist(m$rhat[c("beta.comm", "alpha.comm", "tau.sq.beta", "tau.sq.alpha")]), na.rm = TRUE)
sp_draws <- \(m, term, sp) as.matrix(m$beta.samples)[, paste0(term, "-", sp)]
comm_draws <- \(m, term) as.matrix(m$beta.comm.samples)[, term]
lf_minus_dt <- \(m, sp) sp_draws(m, "Habitat_splitLive_fence", sp) - sp_draws(m, "Habitat_splitDispersed_trees", sp)
## Earlier multi-species fit with pasture as the reference (separate 2016-17 periods, quadratic day of season), for the inflation it showed
ms_old <- readRDS(fit_path("10_boreal_migrants", "oct15_team_day_period_free_ig11"))
## Silvopasture cover within 300 m (%) by silvopasture sub-type, over surveyed location-periods
ssp_by_sub <- round(tapply(ssp_pct[surveyed_lp], matrix(as.character(ss_l$occ.covs$Habitat_split), nrow(surveyed_lp), ncol(surveyed_lp))[surveyed_lp], mean))
## Short names for the text: a species' contrast or coefficient from the single-species (ss_) or multi-species (ms_) fit, formatted with est()
ss_c <- \(sp, k) est(ss_contrasts[[sp]][[k]])
ms_c <- \(sp, k) est(ms_contrasts[[sp]][[k]])
ss_b <- \(sp, term) est(ss_beta[[sp]][, term])
occ_med <- \(x) sprintf("%.2f", median(x))

## Single-species curves along one covariate, one panel per species, with the binned location-period points
ss_plot <- function(curves, points, x_lab, edge = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(curves, aes(x, med, color = Habitat, fill = Habitat))
  if (edge) p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50")
  p + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), alpha = 0.12, color = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(data = points, aes(y = z, size = n), shape = 21, alpha = 0.7, stroke = 0.4, color = "grey20") +
    facet_wrap(~ Species, nrow = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = hab_colors, aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 5, name = "Location-periods") +
    labs(x = x_lab, y = "Occupancy (use) probability") +
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))
}

## Scale of effect: one row of the ring comparison (species or "Community", radius or NA for the fit without canopy, chain length), formatted canopy coefficient (logit, per 10 percentage points of ring cover) and ΔWAIC
ring <- read_csv(ring_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)

## Non-spatial check: the community radius with a location random effect in place of the spatial factor; canopy per 10 percentage points and WAIC against the non-spatial fit without canopy

nonsp_sp <- map(set_names(Migrants), \(sp) sp_draws(ms_nonsp, paste0("Canopy_r", comm_radius), sp) / comm_ring_sd * 10)

## Correlation of the 20 km ring with the 10 km ring over the surveyed location-periods
r_20_10 <- cor(Ring_rows$Canopy_cover_ring[Ring_rows$Radius_m == 20000], Ring_rows$Canopy_cover_ring[Ring_rows$Radius_m == 10000])
```

## Abstract

**Goal:** To understand the impact of silvopasture on the community of Nearctic-Neotropical migrants.

**Motivation:** The multi-species model pools 98 species, so each species' habitat response is pulled toward the community mean, which makes the response of Nearctic-Neotropical migrants harder to determine. The functional trait models (Fig 7, preliminary results report) show that long-distance migrants respond positively to silvopasture (slightly more than resident species, ADD P \> 0), but intervals showed wide uncertainty. Models geared specifically towards migrants allow for more tailored specification, as well as only including surveys conducted during the non-breeding season.

**Methods:** Here I fit a multi-species occupancy model for the community of Nearctic-Neotropical migrants, as well as single-species models for three Nearctic-Neotropical migrants with enough detections (*Setophaga striata, Setophaga ruticilla*, *Piranga rubra*), asking (1) how occupancy differs between pasture, silvopasture and forest, (2) whether it changes with distance to the forest edge, silvopasture cover within 300m and rainfall, and (3) at what scale, if any, migrants respond to woody canopy cover in the surrounding landscape.

**Results:** The community of Nearctic-Neotropical migrants responds positively to silvopasture compared to pasture (community-level mean silvopasture vs pasture contrast `r est(comm_contrasts[["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])`, logit scale), but did not use silvopasture more than forest (`r est(comm_contrasts[["Silvopasture vs forest"]])`). Use was highest at the forest edge, and tended to rise with silvopasture cover within 300 m (`r est(comm_beta[, "ssp"])` per SD). In silvopasture, use tended to rise with annual rainfall more than in pasture (difference in slopes `r est(comm_rain_slopes$Silvopasture - comm_rain_slopes$Pasture)`), the same direction as in the 98-species model, but not clearly. The direction of every silvopasture contrast was robust to the prior on the coefficients, but the size of silvopasture vs pasture was not, because migrants were rarely detected in pasture. Results from the single-species models largely mirrored the multi-species model, which is not surprising given that the vast majority of detections occurred in just these three species. The Blackpoll warbler (*S. striata*), the most commonly detected migrant in our study, responded most strongly to silvopasture: it used silvopasture far more than pasture (`r ss_c("Setophaga_striata", "Silvopasture vs pasture")`) and probably more than forest (`r ss_c("Setophaga_striata", "Silvopasture vs forest")`). It was also the only species with a clear landscape scale, its use declining with woody canopy cover within `r ring_km(striata_radius)` (`r est(striata_canopy)` per 10 percentage points). For the community, canopy cover within `r ring_km(comm_radius)` improved the model because species responded in opposite directions (*S. striata* negatively, *Catharus ustulatus* positively), not through a shared response.

**Conclusions:** Our findings suggest that the community of Nearctic-Neotropical migrants would benefit from converting pasture to silvopasture, although for the average migrant silvopasture does not replace forest. Our findings for the Blackpoll warbler coincide with those of Morales-Rozo et al. (2025), who found higher occupancy in agroforestry systems (shade-grown cacao, citrus, silvopasture) than in native forest, and lower occupancy with more forest within 1 km; here its use likewise declined with landscape canopy cover, at a larger scale (`r ring_km(striata_radius)`).

## Data and model

**Season window.** I used only visits between `r season_start_date` and `r season_end_date`. *S. striata* was first detected in Meta on `r first_detection`, after `r n_visits_before_first` visits without a detection from 23 September to 6 October 2019, and Meta has no April surveys. This leaves `r n_visits` visits at `r n_locations` locations in `r length(Periods_kept)` periods (`r period_text`): `r lp_by_habitat[["Bosque"]]` forest, `r lp_by_habitat[["Ssp"]]` silvopasture and `r lp_by_habitat[["Pastizales"]]` pasture location-periods on `r farms_by_habitat[["Bosque"]]`, `r farms_by_habitat[["Ssp"]]` and `r farms_by_habitat[["Pastizales"]]` farms. The 2016-17 periods surveyed almost only forest, so silvopasture and pasture come from November 2019 and January-February 2026. The same window applies to the multi-species model, so occupancy means wintering use for every species; it drops `r off_season[["Contopus_virens"]]` of *Contopus virens*'s `r off_season[["Contopus_virens"]] + detections[["Contopus_virens"]]` detections and `r off_season[["Catharus_ustulatus"]]` of *Catharus ustulatus*'s `r off_season[["Catharus_ustulatus"]] + detections[["Catharus_ustulatus"]]`, mostly birds on passage in September and October.

**Single-species models.** I fit a multi-season spatial occupancy model (`spOccupancy::stPGOcc`) for each of the three migrants detected often enough outside forest, with Bernoulli occupancy and detection and logit links. Occupancy depends on habitat (forest as the reference), annual rainfall, distance from the forest edge, silvopasture cover within 300 m and survey period, and for *S. striata* also on woody canopy cover within `r ring_km(striata_radius)` ([Scale of effect of landscape canopy cover](#sec-scale); no radius improved the *S. ruticilla* or *P. rubra* models). Distance enters as a hinge, with one term for distance outside forest and one for depth inside forest, so that the two sides of the edge can have different slopes. Each survey period has its own intercept (2025-26 as reference; the two 2016-17 periods share one), so habitat contrasts come from habitats surveyed in the same period rather than from differences between years. Instead of a linear day of season, occupancy includes an arrival-period indicator, 1 for location-periods whose mean date falls before 1 December. eBird Status and Trends shows *S. striata*'s non-breeding distribution settled in South America by late November to early December, and *S. striata* arrives later than most other migrants, so the date is conservative for the community. With period intercepts, a linear day of season varied within periods almost only between October-December 2016 and March 2017, both forest only, so its slope was one forest contrast extended across the whole season; it predicted occupancy rising steadily from October to March, which is not plausible for wintering birds. The arrival indicator is estimated from the same 2016-17 forest data (all November 2019 location-periods fall before 1 December, so in 2019 it is absorbed by that period's intercept). Use was lower during arrival for *S. striata* (`r est(arrival_ss$Setophaga_striata)`), less clearly for *S. ruticilla* (`r est(arrival_ss$Setophaga_ruticilla)`), and not for *P. rubra* (`r est(arrival_ss$Piranga_rubra)`). The choice of season term left every habitat contrast unchanged; WAIC with a linear day of season, no season term and the arrival indicator was `r paste(map_chr(names(season_waic), \(k) paste0(if (k == "Community") "multi-species model" else paste0("*", species_label(k), "*"), " ", paste(sprintf("%.1f", season_waic[[k]]), collapse = " / "))), collapse = "; ")` (the multi-species arrival fit with doubled chains). An arrival period ending 1 November, where per-visit detection of any migrant in forest jumped in our data, could not be estimated: *S. striata*, *S. ruticilla* and *Mniotilta varia* were never detected before it, so their arrival coefficients drifted to extreme values (e.g. *S. striata* `r sprintf("%.1f", arrnov_sp[["Setophaga_striata"]])`) and the among-species variance of the arrival coefficient did not converge (Rhat `r sprintf("%.2f", arrnov_rhat)`). The sensitivity fits below still include a linear day of season. Annual rainfall enters additively: it varies only between farms (`r farms_by_habitat[["Ssp"]]` silvopasture farms), and its interaction with habitat reversed sign when annual rainfall was replaced by driest-month rainfall.

Detection depends on whether the point is in forest, the start time of the count and its square, and the collector team, with a team-specific slope of log sampling day that lets each team's detection improve over its first days in the field (warm-up). Only `r length(Teams)` teams surveyed within the season window, too few to estimate a random effect, so teams enter as fixed effects.

A spatial random effect absorbs residual spatial autocorrelation in occupancy: a nearest-neighbour Gaussian process (NNGP, which approximates a full Gaussian process by conditioning each location on its 5 nearest neighbours) with an exponential correlation function and an effective range free between `r free_range_km[1]` and `r free_range_km[2]` km, the largest distance between locations. Each model ran `r Mcmc$n.chains` chains of `r format(n_iter, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` iterations (`r format(Mcmc$n.burn, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` burn-in, thinned by `r Mcmc$n.thin`); the largest Rhat across all parameters of the three fits was `r sprintf("%.2f", max_rhat_ss)`.

**Multi-species model.** I also fit a multi-species model (`spOccupancy::svcTMsPGOcc`) of the `r length(Migrants)` Nearctic-Neotropical migrants with at least 2 in-season detections (Table 1), with the same covariates plus canopy cover within `r ring_km(comm_radius)` ([Scale of effect of landscape canopy cover](#sec-scale)), and chains twice as long (`r format(n_iter_long, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` iterations, `r format(Mcmc_long$n.burn, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` burn-in, thinned by `r Mcmc_long$n.thin`), as the among-species variance of the silvopasture coefficient mixed poorly at the standard length. Each species' coefficients are drawn from a community normal distribution, whose mean describes the average migrant and whose variance (inverse-gamma(1, 1) prior) sets how strongly species are pulled toward that mean; one spatial factor shares spatial structure among species. Six of the ten species have at most `r max(detections[!names(detections) %in% c(species_ss, "Catharus_ustulatus")])` detections, so their estimates rest mostly on the community mean, and the model's main use is to check the single-species results and to estimate the community mean. The largest community-level Rhat was `r sprintf("%.2f", max_rhat_comm)`, and `r if (n_sp_rhat == 0) "no" else n_sp_rhat` species coefficients had Rhat above 1.1.

**Occupancy as use.** Visits within a location-period can be up to about two weeks apart, and wintering migrants may move among points over that time. If they do, closure is violated: the occupancy probability estimates the probability that a location was *used* during the location-period, and detection estimates availability times detectability (Rota et al. 2009). Occupancy below is read as use of a location during the non-breeding season.

**Notation.** Estimates are given as the posterior median followed by the 95% credible interval (CrI), and in the text by the posterior probability that the quantity is positive, e.g. `r est(ss_contrasts$Setophaga_striata[["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])` for *S. striata*'s silvopasture vs pasture contrast on the logit scale.

## Habitat

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data
#| tbl-cap: "Nearctic-Neotropical migrants in the multi-species model: visits with a detection within the season window, and location-periods with a detection in each habitat. Asterisk: species also fit with a single-species model."
kable(data_tbl)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-habitat
#| fig-cap: !expr habitat_cap
#| fig-height: 3.2
ggplot(occ_by_habitat, aes(Habitat, med, color = Habitat)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Species, nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = hab_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Occupancy (use) probability") +
  theme_bw() + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

*S. striata* used silvopasture far more than pasture (`r ss_c("Setophaga_striata", "Silvopasture vs pasture")`) and probably more than forest (`r ss_c("Setophaga_striata", "Silvopasture vs forest")`), in line with Morales-Rozo et al. (2025). *S. ruticilla* also used silvopasture more than pasture (`r ss_c("Setophaga_ruticilla", "Silvopasture vs pasture")`), but tended to use forest more than silvopasture (`r ss_c("Setophaga_ruticilla", "Silvopasture vs forest")`). *P. rubra*'s habitat contrasts were uncertain (silvopasture vs pasture `r ss_c("Piranga_rubra", "Silvopasture vs pasture")`).

The size of every contrast against pasture should be read with caution. Only `r det_lp_by_habitat$Setophaga_striata[["Pastizales"]]` of `r lp_by_habitat[["Pastizales"]]` pasture location-periods had an *S. striata* detection, so pasture occupancy is weakly identified and partly set by the prior. Refitting *S. striata* with pasture instead of forest as the reference level, which changes only which coefficients the priors act on, gave a silvopasture vs pasture contrast of `r est(striata_pref[, "HabitatSsp"])` instead of `r est(striata_nc_contrasts[["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])` (both without canopy cover); the earlier fit with separate 2016-17 periods and a quadratic in day of season gave `r est(striata_old[, "HabitatSsp"])`, so the reference level, not the period or season terms, moves it. The direction is robust, and silvopasture vs forest barely changed (`r est(striata_pref[, "HabitatSsp"] - striata_pref[, "HabitatBosque"])` with pasture as reference).

Varying the prior directly gives the same picture. With the variance of the normal prior on the coefficients set to `r prior_vars[1]` and `r prior_vars[2]` instead of the default 2.72, *S. striata*'s silvopasture vs pasture contrast was `r est(striata_prior[["1"]][["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])` and `r est(striata_prior[["10"]][["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])` (default `r est(striata_nc_contrasts[["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])`; all three fits without canopy cover), and silvopasture vs forest `r est(striata_prior[["1"]][["Silvopasture vs forest"]])` and `r est(striata_prior[["10"]][["Silvopasture vs forest"]])`. In the multi-species model, with the same variances on the prior for the community-level means, the community-level mean silvopasture vs pasture contrast was `r est(comm_prior[["10"]][["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])` at variance `r prior_vars[2]`; at variance `r prior_vars[1]` the among-species variance of the silvopasture coefficient did not converge (Rhat `r sprintf("%.2f", rhat_ssp_var[["1"]])`), so that fit is not interpreted. The direction of every silvopasture contrast is robust to the prior; the size of silvopasture vs pasture is not.

The multi-species model agrees with the single-species models (@fig-compare). For *S. striata*, silvopasture vs pasture was `r ms_c("Setophaga_striata", "Silvopasture vs pasture")` and silvopasture vs forest `r ms_c("Setophaga_striata", "Silvopasture vs forest")`, against a community mean of `r est(comm_contrasts[["Silvopasture vs pasture"]])` and `r est(comm_contrasts[["Silvopasture vs forest"]])`. The average Nearctic-Neotropical migrant thus used silvopasture more than pasture but not more than forest, and *S. striata* stands out from the community by using silvopasture more than forest.

```{r}
#| label: fig-compare
#| fig-cap: !expr compare_cap
#| fig-height: 3.4
ggplot(compare_tbl, aes(med, Species, color = Model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lcl, xmax = ucl), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Contrast, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`Single-species` = "grey30", `Multi-species` = "#6250d6"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Contrast (logit scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(face = c("plain", rep("italic", length(species_ss)))))
```

## Landscape context

```{r}
#| label: fig-context
#| fig-cap: !expr context_cap
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot(context_comm, aes(x, med, color = Habitat, fill = Habitat)) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(Panel = factor(context_specs$Panel[2], context_specs$Panel)), aes(xintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(data = context_species, aes(group = interaction(Species, Habitat)), linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Panel, scales = "free_x", strip.position = "bottom", labeller = label_wrap_gen(22)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = hab_colors, aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Occupancy (use) probability", color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top", strip.placement = "outside", strip.background = element_blank())
```

**Rainfall.** In the multi-species model with a habitat-by-rainfall interaction (`r format(n_iter_mid, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` iterations per chain; largest community-level Rhat `r sprintf("%.2f", rhat_comm(ms_rain))`), the community-level mean of the species' rainfall slopes (logit scale, per SD of annual rainfall, `r round(prec_scale$SD)` mm) was `r est(comm_rain_slopes$Silvopasture)` in silvopasture, `r est(comm_rain_slopes$Pasture)` in pasture and `r est(comm_rain_slopes$Forest)` in forest (@fig-context a). The silvopasture slope exceeded the pasture slope by `r est(comm_rain_slopes$Silvopasture - comm_rain_slopes$Pasture)`, the same direction as the habitat-by-rainfall interaction in the 98-species model, but not clearly, and the interaction did not improve WAIC (`r sprintf("%.1f", waic[["rain"]])` vs `r sprintf("%.1f", waic[["base"]])` for the additive model). The single-species fits agree in direction: the silvopasture slope was positive for all three species, clearly only for *S. ruticilla* (*S. striata* `r est(ss_rain_slopes$Setophaga_striata$Silvopasture)`, *S. ruticilla* `r est(ss_rain_slopes$Setophaga_ruticilla$Silvopasture)`, *P. rubra* `r est(ss_rain_slopes$Piranga_rubra$Silvopasture)`), while the pasture slopes spanned zero (@fig-rain-ss). Their forest slopes (`r paste(map_chr(species_ss, \(sp) sprintf("%.2f", median(ss_rain_slopes[[sp]]$Forest))), collapse = ", ")`) are steeper than the same species' forest slopes in the multi-species model (`r paste(map_chr(species_ss, \(sp) sprintf("%.2f", median(ms_rain_beta[[sp]][, "Tot_prec"]))), collapse = ", ")`), which are pulled toward the community-level mean forest slope set mostly by the rarely detected, forest-only species. Rainfall varies only between farms, so each silvopasture slope rests on `r farms_by_habitat[["Ssp"]]` farms.

**Distance to the forest edge and silvopasture cover.** In the additive multi-species model, the community-level mean slope with distance outside forest (shared by pasture and silvopasture) was `r est(comm_beta[, "Dist_open"])` per SD (`r round(dist_sd_m)` m), and with depth inside forest `r est(comm_beta[, "Dist_inside"])`: the average migrant's use was highest at the forest edge (@fig-context b). The community-level mean slope of silvopasture cover within 300 m was `r est(comm_beta[, "ssp"])` per SD (`r round(ssp_scale$SD)` percentage points) (@fig-context c). Use changed little with woody canopy cover within `r ring_km(comm_radius)` for the average migrant (community-level mean `r est(ms_ring_sp_comm)` per 10 percentage points), but species differed in direction (@fig-context d; [Scale of effect of landscape canopy cover](#sec-scale)).

Among the single-species fits, use rose with silvopasture cover within 300 m for *P. rubra* (`r ss_b("Piranga_rubra", "ssp")`) and *S. striata* (`r ss_b("Setophaga_striata", "ssp")`), but not clearly for *S. ruticilla* (`r ss_b("Setophaga_ruticilla", "ssp")`) (@fig-ssp). Outside forest, use declined away from the forest edge for *S. ruticilla* (`r ss_b("Setophaga_ruticilla", "Dist_open")`) and tended to for *P. rubra* (`r ss_b("Piranga_rubra", "Dist_open")`), but not for *S. striata* (`r ss_b("Setophaga_striata", "Dist_open")`), whose use instead tended to decline with depth inside forest (`r ss_b("Setophaga_striata", "Dist_inside")`) (@fig-dist).

## Scale of effect of landscape canopy cover {#sec-scale}

**Approach.** Morales-Rozo et al. (2025) found lower *S. striata* occupancy with more forest within 1 km. To find the scale at which migrants respond to landscape tree cover, I added woody canopy cover (survey-year maps) in a ring around each point to the additive models above, one fit per outer radius: the `r length(Ring_radii_m) - 1` radii of the 98-species scale-of-effect fits (`r min(Ring_radii_m)` m to 10 km) and 20 km, since migrants may perceive the landscape at large scales, though the study extent (at most `r free_range_km[2]` km between locations) leaves little contrast beyond that: the 20 km ring correlates `r sprintf("%.2f", r_20_10)` with the 10 km ring. Rings exclude the inner 50 m, so they do not duplicate the point's own habitat, and each radius is standardised over the `r nrow(Stacked_oc)` surveyed location-periods of the 98-species data. Each fit was compared by WAIC with the same model without canopy. To save time these fits used `r format(n_iter_short, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`-iteration chains; the community's two best radii and *S. striata*'s best radius were refit with the full chains. The profiles were fit before day of season was dropped, so they include it; the chosen radii were then refit with the arrival indicator as the base models.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ring
#| fig-cap: !expr ring_cap
#| fig-height: 5.5
ring %>%
  filter(!is.na(Radius_m), Chains == "short") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(dWAIC, Canopy_median), names_to = "name", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(lo = if_else(name == "dWAIC", NA_real_, Canopy_lo), hi = if_else(name == "dWAIC", NA_real_, Canopy_hi),
         name = recode(name, dWAIC = "WAIC minus WAIC without canopy", Canopy_median = "Canopy coefficient (logit, per 10 percentage points)"),
         Species = str_replace(Species, "_", " ")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Radius_m / 1000, y = value, colour = Species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.08), na.rm = TRUE, size = 0.3) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.08)) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Outer ring radius (km)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

**Results.** *S. striata* has the only clear single-species scale (@fig-ring): WAIC falls smoothly from 1 km to a minimum at `r ring_km(ring_best("Setophaga_striata")$Radius_m)` (ΔWAIC `r ring_dw("Setophaga_striata", striata_radius)`) and rises again beyond 7.5 km, and its use *declines* with landscape canopy cover (`r ring_est(ring_row("Setophaga_striata", striata_radius))` per 10 percentage points at `r ring_km(striata_radius)`), consistent with Morales-Rozo et al. (2025). For *S. ruticilla*, no radius up to 10 km changed WAIC by more than `r sprintf("%.0f", max(abs(filter(ring, Species == "Setophaga_ruticilla", Chains == "short", Radius_m <= 10000)$dWAIC)))`; only the 20 km ring improved it (ΔWAIC `r ring_dw("Setophaga_ruticilla", 20000)`, canopy `r ring_est(ring_row("Setophaga_ruticilla", 20000))`), a nearly between-farm gradient that I do not trust as a scale of effect. *P. rubra*'s profile is flat within run-to-run noise (ΔWAIC `r sprintf("%.1f", min(filter(ring, Species == "Piranga_rubra", Chains == "short")$dWAIC))` at best), with positive but unclear coefficients. Canopy cover is therefore left out of the *S. ruticilla* and *P. rubra* models. In *S. striata*'s base model (full-length chains), the `r ring_km(striata_radius)` ring gave a canopy coefficient of `r est(striata_canopy)` per 10 percentage points (ΔWAIC `r sprintf("%.1f", striata_dwaic)` against the same model without canopy).

For the community, WAIC improved most at `r ring_km(ring_best("Community")$Radius_m)` (ΔWAIC `r ring_dw("Community", comm_radius)`; `r ring_dw("Community", comm_radius, "full")` with full chains), with 2 and 5 km close behind. In the base multi-species model, the community-level mean canopy coefficient was negative but unclear (`r est(ms_ring_sp_comm)` per 10 percentage points), and the among-species SD of the canopy coefficient was large (`r ci(ms_ring_tau_sd)`): the model gains from canopy because species respond differently, not through a shared response. *S. striata* (`r est(ms_ring_sp$Setophaga_striata)`) and *C. ustulatus* (`r est(ms_ring_sp$Catharus_ustulatus)`) respond in opposite directions, while *S. ruticilla* (`r est(ms_ring_sp$Setophaga_ruticilla)`) and *P. rubra* (`r est(ms_ring_sp$Piranga_rubra)`) tend to respond positively, and the six rare species lean negative with wide intervals.

**Canopy cover and the spatial random effect.** Landscape canopy at a few km varies mostly between farms, so it can compete with the spatial random effect. In the single-species fits the spatial variance is weakly identified (95% CrIs about 0.2 to 4 in every fit), but for *S. striata* adding canopy at `r ring_km(striata_radius)` lowered its posterior median from `r sprintf("%.2f", ring_row("Setophaga_striata", NA)$Spatial_var)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", ring_row("Setophaga_striata", striata_radius)$Spatial_var)` and the SD across locations of the posterior-mean spatial effect from `r sprintf("%.2f", ring_row("Setophaga_striata", NA)$SD_w_sites)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", ring_row("Setophaga_striata", striata_radius)$SD_w_sites)`: canopy explains part of the spatial pattern the random effect carried without it. Both returned to their baseline values at 20 km, where the canopy coefficient was near zero. For *S. ruticilla* and *P. rubra* the spatial effect did not change. In the multi-species model, the shared spatial factor's effective range shortened from `r sprintf("%.1f", ring_row("Community", NA, "full")$Range_km)` km without canopy to `r sprintf("%.1f", ring_row("Community", comm_radius, "full")$Range_km)` km at `r ring_km(comm_radius)` (95% CrIs span most of the prior in both), and *S. ruticilla*'s spatial variance (its loading squared) rose from `r sprintf("%.2f", ring_loading("Setophaga_ruticilla", NA)$Spatial_var)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", ring_loading("Setophaga_ruticilla", comm_radius)$Spatial_var)`: with canopy taking up the broad pattern, the factor describes finer-scale structure that *S. ruticilla* shares. *S. striata*'s loading is fixed at 1 for identifiability, so its spatial variance cannot change in this model. Without the spatial random effect (a location random effect in its place), the `r ring_km(comm_radius)` ring still improved WAIC (ΔWAIC `r sprintf("%.1f", nonsp_dwaic)` against the same model without canopy), and the canopy coefficients barely changed: community-level mean `r est(nonsp_comm)`, *S. striata* `r est(nonsp_sp$Setophaga_striata)`, *C. ustulatus* `r est(nonsp_sp$Catharus_ustulatus)` per 10 percentage points. The canopy effect therefore does not depend on the spatial random effect it partly replaces.

## Nearctic-Neotropical migrant multi-species model

**Why the first multi-species fit inflated the contrasts.** An earlier fit with pasture as the reference level gave larger contrasts against pasture than the single-species models (e.g. *S. striata* silvopasture vs pasture `r est(sp_draws(ms_old, "HabitatSsp", "Setophaga_striata"))` against `r est(striata_old[, "HabitatSsp"])` single-species). Its silvopasture and forest occupancy matched the single-species fits, but each species' pasture occupancy, then the intercept, was pulled toward a low community intercept set by the six rare species, which were detected almost only in forest. With forest, the best-sampled habitat, as the reference, the contrasts agree (@fig-compare), and pasture occupancy under the prediction conditions is low in both models, with no consistent shift between them (*S. striata* `r occ_med(pasture_occ$Setophaga_striata$ss)` single-species vs `r occ_med(pasture_occ$Setophaga_striata$ms)` multi-species; *S. ruticilla* `r occ_med(pasture_occ$Setophaga_ruticilla$ss)` vs `r occ_med(pasture_occ$Setophaga_ruticilla$ms)`; *P. rubra* `r occ_med(pasture_occ$Piranga_rubra$ss)` vs `r occ_med(pasture_occ$Piranga_rubra$ms)`). The earlier fit also did not converge, because March 2017 surveyed only forest and its period intercept was not identified for species never detected then; merging the two 2016-17 periods fixed this in the base model (without canopy, the largest community-level Rhat left, `r sprintf("%.2f", rhat_comm(ms_fit_nc))`, is for the among-species variance of one team's warm-up slope in detection).

**Silvopasture's own slope with distance from the forest edge.** In the models above, pasture and silvopasture share one slope with distance outside forest. Letting silvopasture differ from pasture, the community-mean difference was `r est(comm_draws(ms_dist, "Ssp_Dist_open"))`, and all three well-detected species had flatter slopes in silvopasture than in pasture, though none clearly (*S. striata* `r est(sp_draws(ms_dist, "Ssp_Dist_open", "Setophaga_striata"))`, *S. ruticilla* `r est(sp_draws(ms_dist, "Ssp_Dist_open", "Setophaga_ruticilla"))`, *P. rubra* `r est(sp_draws(ms_dist, "Ssp_Dist_open", "Piranga_rubra"))`). WAIC did not change (`r sprintf("%.1f", waic[["dist"]])` vs `r sprintf("%.1f", waic[["base"]])`), and the largest community-level Rhat was `r sprintf("%.2f", rhat_comm(ms_dist))`, for the among-species variance of the 2016-17 period intercept rather than the slope terms.

**Live fences vs dispersed trees.** Splitting silvopasture into live fences (`r sum(ss_l$occ.covs$Habitat_split == "Live_fence")` locations within the season window) and dispersed trees (`r sum(ss_l$occ.covs$Habitat_split == "Dispersed_trees")`) asks more than the migrant data can answer: the among-species variance of the dispersed-trees effect did not converge (Rhat `r sprintf("%.2f", ms_split$rhat$tau.sq.beta[colnames(ms_split$tau.sq.beta.samples) == "Habitat_splitDispersed_trees"])`), and WAIC did not change (`r sprintf("%.1f", waic[["split"]])`). *S. striata* tended to use dispersed trees more than live fences (live fence minus dispersed trees `r est(lf_minus_dt(ms_split, "Setophaga_striata"))`), which fits its higher use with more silvopasture cover nearby, since dispersed-tree points have more silvopasture cover within 300 m than live-fence points (mean `r ssp_by_sub[["Dispersed_trees"]]`% vs `r ssp_by_sub[["Live_fence"]]`% over surveyed location-periods). The split is better tested in the 98-species model.

## Nearctic-Neotropical migrants outside Meta

Extending the models to other regions would add few detections outside forest. Within the same season window, the other ecoregions have `r out_effort[["Ssp"]]` silvopasture and `r out_effort[["Pastizales"]]` pasture visits, against `r out_effort[["Bosque"]]` in forest, and `r out_forest[["forest"]]` of the `r out_forest[["all"]]` visits with a Nearctic-Neotropical migrant outside Meta were in forest (@tbl-outside; survey effort in @tbl-effort). The main gains would be *Setophaga fusca*, an Andean winterer detected mostly in Eje Cafetero forest, and more forest data for *P. rubra* and *C. ustulatus*; *S. striata* was not recorded outside Meta in season.

## Next steps

- Check the season window against eBird arrival and departure dates in Meta.
- Test closure: does detection on a visit depend on the days since the previous visit to the same location-period?
- Season-specific rainfall from CHIRPS (Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data; free, daily to monthly, about 5 km resolution) to test whether *S. striata* shifts habitat in drier years.
